contexts.title: Defined C and a bounded record tool
contexts.problem: A record is useful only if every byte access, lifetime and arithmetic operation is defined. Establish these obligations before selecting a container.

contexts.title: Ordered records and bounded lookup
contexts.problem: Filtering, deduplication and range queries demand explicit comparator and ownership contracts. Compare linear scans, sorted views and hashing on the same records.

contexts.title: Incremental input and owned publication
contexts.problem: File, socket and device input arrives in fragments. A finite queue must preserve unread bytes, expose pressure and publish only complete records.

contexts.title: Configuration, symbols and reusable interfaces
contexts.problem: Configuration keys and runtime symbols need stable identity while storage may move or rehash. Distinguish equality, address identity and ownership.

contexts.title: Deadlines, dispatch and overload
contexts.problem: An event service must find due work, cancel stale registrations and bound retention. A changing operation mix motivates a representation change.

contexts.title: Allocation and durable indexed storage
contexts.problem: A growing store must account for allocation failure, fragmentation, page I/O and recovery. A successful in-memory update is not durable publication.

contexts.title: Compilation and dependency processing
contexts.problem: Build dependencies, control flow and incremental computation form graphs. Cycles, reachability and fixed points impose different contracts.

contexts.title: Telemetry and numerical processing
contexts.problem: A stream of observations needs bounded history, stable numerical meaning and honest uncertainty. Select summaries using the query and error contract.

contexts.title: Concurrent state and machine boundaries
contexts.problem: Sharing a component changes the proof: publication order, borrower lifetime and reclamation become separate obligations.

contexts.title: Firmware and kernel integration
contexts.problem: Portable mechanisms meet reset, interrupt, DMA and ABI contracts. Preserve freestanding boundaries and qualify every reused artifact on its consumer target.

contexts.title: Native measurements and causal diagnosis
contexts.problem: A timing difference must survive equal semantics, generated-code inspection and a defensible observation boundary. Hardware events answer narrower questions than their names suggest.

contexts.title: Independent system selection and transfer
contexts.problem: An unfamiliar service workload must be decomposed into explicit contracts. Select and reject mechanisms using evidence, then revise them under a changed assumption.

Complete the integrated service with assessed learner producers or clearly identified supplied reference adapters; a rigorous inconclusive attribution is acceptable. nodes.why_now: A hashed timer wheel under changed precision (step 1 of 2). Many timers with coarse acceptable precision make even logarithmic heap repair look avoidable. Bucket placement modulo the wheel size is not due identity, and generation reuse can resurrect a cancelled ID. At now 0 a delay-5 timer maps to bucket 1 but must not fire at tick 1; it fires exactly at 5. As the changed-assumption encounter for deadline collections: Derive bucket index, full due identity, list invariants and generation retirement; a delay-5 timer in bucket 1 must not fire at tick 1.

episodes.title: A first defined C diagnostic and a reproducible build

entering_state.summary: No accepted work. The learner can edit text and run a shell.

episodes.motivating_limitation: Nothing yet distinguishes a compile error from a link, load or input failure, and no argument or result is reproducible. A record tool cannot be trusted while its bounds, sequencing and build provenance are guesses.

notes.U-T01-02-01: Classify indices -1, 0, 2, 3 and 4 for a three-element traversal before any conversion, and repair the analysis-only off-by-one and uninitialized cases.
notes.U-T01-03-01: Separate syntax rejection, a missing definition at link, a loader mismatch and a tool rejecting malformed input; they are different failures.
notes.U-T01-03-03: Specify the at-most-four-token grammar with separate empty, malformed, range, capacity and prefix-overflow statuses, then inject and minimize a check-after-add defect.

exiting_artifact.description: The bounded signed-decimal record tool (records.tool) with a partitioned specification, a minimized regression and a provenance manifest.
exiting_artifact.competence: The bounded signed-decimal record tool (records.tool) with a partitioned specification, a minimized regression and a provenance manifest.

episodes.transition_reason: Every later increment is built, run and diagnosed with this habit; the next episode makes the compiler pipeline itself an object of evidence.

episodes.title: Build stages, targets and a diagnostics policy

entering_state.summary: A reproducible record tool and its provenance manifest.

episodes.motivating_limitation: A green build is still not evidence: a stale preprocessed file, a mislabeled cross-target object or a blanket warning suppression can survive a passing run.

notes.U-T07-01-01: Retain step.i, change BIAS from 7 to 9 and locate where the old value survives.
notes.U-T07-01-03: A nonzero compiler exit is not a validated negative test: inject a nonexistent compiler and a missing include and require the runner to reject them.

exiting_artifact.description: An artifact manifest that records stages, target triple, data model and selected startup files, plus a compile-case runner that distinguishes intended diagnostics from infrastructure failure.
exiting_artifact.competence: An artifact manifest that records stages, target triple, data model and selected startup files, plus a compile-case runner that distinguishes intended diagnostics from infrastructure failure.

episodes.transition_reason: Cost and measurement work later reuse this manifest; checked arithmetic comes next because every extent computation depends on it.

episodes.title: Checked arithmetic before any extent

entering_state.summary: A reproducible build and a specified record tool.

episodes.motivating_limitation: The record tool already multiplies counts by widths and adds prefixes. Without a derived admission check, a wrapped size silently becomes a short buffer.

notes.U-T04-01-03: Enumerate every synthetic 8-bit operand pair against a wider exact oracle; testing the wrapped result is the rejected method.
notes.U-T04-01-04: Reject divisor zero and the minimum/-1 pair before both division and remainder, then export bytes.checked.
notes.X-T04-001: Transfer the guards to extent admission: admit a signed count only after proving its magnitude fits size_t, and preserve output on every rejection.

exiting_artifact.description: bytes.checked: finite-width add/subtract/multiply and prefix+count*width guards that leave outputs unchanged on failure, and a transactional extent admission.
exiting_artifact.competence: bytes.checked: finite-width add/subtract/multiply and prefix+count*width guards that leave outputs unchanged on failure, and a transactional extent admission.

episodes.transition_reason: Next, the subject changes from integer values to objects: a checked extent says nothing about whether the storage it measures is declared, alive or aligned, so declarations, lifetime and alignment come before any pointer is formed.

episodes.title: Declarations, object lifetime and alignment

entering_state.summary: Checked arithmetic is available; pointers are not yet trusted.

episodes.motivating_limitation: A borrowed view is only meaningful if its declaration, the lifetime of the object it names and the alignment of its base are known. An unchanged numeric address does not keep an allocation alive.

notes.U-T03-01-01: Track an allocation across failed resize and successful relocation without evaluating the old pointer after its lifetime ends.
notes.U-T03-01-03: Explain why uintptr_t modulo is not an unconditional ISO alignment validator.

exiting_artifact.description: Lifetime timelines for automatic, static, thread-local and allocated records, a padding/representation ledger and an aligned-storage interface that separates capacity, alignment, type and owner.
exiting_artifact.competence: Lifetime timelines for automatic, static, thread-local and allocated records, a padding/representation ledger and an aligned-storage interface that separates capacity, alignment, type and owner.

episodes.transition_reason: The next episode forms derived pointers into live arrays. Its admission checks need exactly these premises: the object is alive, its declaration gives the element type and its base is aligned.

episodes.title: Borrowed cursors over live arrays

entering_state.summary: Checked extents plus object lifetime and alignment arguments.

episodes.motivating_limitation: Every parser and container ahead walks a borrowed region. Checking an index after forming base+offset is too late, and null-plus-zero is not ordinary pointer arithmetic.

notes.X-T03-001: Prove cursor indices and subview extents inside the backing array before forming any derived pointer, then export foundation.cursor.
notes.U-T03-02-01: Consume the exported cursor: a matrix is an array of row arrays, not row pointers, and contiguous bytes do not erase subobject bounds.

exiting_artifact.description: foundation.cursor (struct fd_cursor, fd_take, fd_subview) and bytes.cursor: borrowed byte regions with checked remaining length whose failed reads preserve the cursor.
exiting_artifact.competence: foundation.cursor (struct fd_cursor, fd_take, fd_subview) and bytes.cursor: borrowed byte regions with checked remaining length whose failed reads preserve the cursor.

episodes.transition_reason: With defined indexing and checked arithmetic available, the algorithmic vocabulary can be stated as proofs about real C operations.

episodes.title: Invariants, termination and cost on the record tool

entering_state.summary: Defined indexing (bytes.cursor) and checked arithmetic (bytes.checked).

episodes.motivating_limitation: The record tool computes prefix sums and selections, but nothing yet proves that a loop establishes its postcondition, terminates, or keeps every intermediate representable.

notes.U-T01-01-01: Prove the staged-prefix invariant and termination; explain why [INT_MAX,1,-1] must reject before addition even though its mathematical sum fits.
notes.U-T01-01-02: Separate digit representation from byte order and a representable final sum from an invalid signed intermediate.

exiting_artifact.description: Stated invariants with initialization, preservation and exit, decreasing termination measures, and separate work/auxiliary-storage accounts for the staged-prefix contract.
exiting_artifact.competence: Stated invariants with initialization, preservation and exit, decreasing termination measures, and separate work/auxiliary-storage accounts for the staged-prefix contract.

episodes.transition_reason: Containers come next; each must state its representation invariant in this vocabulary before it is implemented.

episodes.title: Function contracts, result types and enforcement

entering_state.summary: Checked arithmetic, borrowed cursors and loop invariants.

episodes.motivating_limitation: Upcoming components return partial progress, failure and found-zero results. A sentinel-only interface or a side-effecting assert cannot express these outcomes.

notes.U-T18-01-02: Prove n <= cap-len only after len <= cap; len+n <= cap can wrap before admission.
notes.U-T18-01-04: Separate required evaluation from an optional assertion and prove invalid inputs never commit under NDEBUG on or off.

exiting_artifact.description: Contracts that partition admissible states, append invariants proven without wrapping, explicit result types with defined failed-output state, and a classification of each obligation as compile-time, runtime, assertion or test.
exiting_artifact.competence: Contracts that partition admissible states, append invariants proven without wrapping, explicit result types with defined failed-output state, and a classification of each obligation as compile-time, runtime, assertion or test.

episodes.transition_reason: The next episode stores data for the first time. A sequence over caller-owned storage must return partial progress and failure with the result and failed-output conventions set here, rather than sentinels.

episodes.title: Logical sequences over caller-owned storage

theory.title: Loop invariants and induction
theory.reasoning: State an invariant strong enough to establish the postcondition, prove initialization, preservation and exit, and keep representability of every intermediate as a separate obligation.

bindings.rejects: A final mathematical sum or loop invariant is mistaken for representable intermediates or termination.
bindings.reasoning: Staged prefixes: at step k, staged[0..k) are representable prefixes; [INT_MAX,1,-1] rejects before addition although its final sum fits.

bindings.rejects: Any true loop property is sufficient as an invariant.
bindings.reasoning: Derive 0<=i<=n and acc=sum(a[0..i)) with 0<=acc<=10i; show that acc<=40 is true but cannot establish the final sum.

bindings.rejects: Testing n in 0..4 is an inductive proof of arbitrary length.
bindings.reasoning: Prove initialization, preservation and exit for the summing loop, then delete the increment and name the exact failing obligation.

theory.title: Termination measures and resource bounds
theory.reasoning: Exhibit a nonnegative measure that strictly decreases on every back edge of the actual code under admitted input, and derive the resulting operation and stack bounds.

bindings.rejects: A loop that usually terminates has a proof of progress.
bindings.reasoning: Half-open lower_bound with hi-lo as the decreasing measure on empty, singleton and all-equal arrays.

bindings.rejects: A loop bound stated in English proves termination of the actual code.
bindings.reasoning: Use n-i as a variant, derive n reads, n adds and constant stack, and show how unsigned underflow invalidates a careless variant.

theory.title: Recurrences for divide-and-conquer work and depth
theory.reasoning: Write the work and depth recurrences from the implemented split, including uneven halves and adversarial partitions, and solve each separately rather than quoting an average-case class.

bindings.rejects: Bounded recursion alone gives O(n log n) work.
bindings.reasoning: Smaller-side recursion bounds the depth recurrence while an adversarial pivot still yields the quadratic work recurrence W(n)=W(n-1)+n-1 without a fallback.

bindings.rejects: A randomized pivot alone gives a deterministic worst-case bound.
bindings.reasoning: With a depth budget the combined bound is partition work before fallback plus the heap-sort bound; the expected-case recurrence of a randomized pivot is not a worst-case bound.

bindings.rejects: treats odd n as equal halves
bindings.reasoning: Top-down stable merge: W(1)=0 and W(n)=W(ceil(n/2))+W(floor(n/2))+n-1, so W(7)=14 with recursion depth 3, not n log2 n.

theory.title: Aggregate, accounting and potential arguments
theory.reasoning: Charge copies to growth with a potential function, keep the initial potential in the telescoping sum, and separate the amortized sequence bound from single-operation latency, failed attempts and variable copy weights.

bindings.rejects: An empty-state proof is reused for a negative or nonzero initial potential.
bindings.reasoning: Phi=2*live-capacity from live=5, capacity=8 through the next growth; live=1, capacity=8 starts negative.

bindings.rejects: Amortized constant append guarantees constant per-call latency and stable addresses.
bindings.reasoning: Appends 1..8 with capacities 1,2,4,8 copy 1+2+4=7 old elements, while one append can move the whole prefix and invalidate borrows.

bindings.rejects: Amortized constant insertion implies bounded allocator latency, destructor time or response time.
bindings.reasoning: Variable-size deep copies change the copy weights of the doubling proof; the guarantee is deterministic over the sequence, not probabilistic, and excludes allocator latency.

theory.title: Greedy choice and exchange arguments
theory.reasoning: Prove that exchanging the first choice of an optimal solution for the greedy choice preserves feasibility and value, and falsify plausible alternative rules with small counterexamples.

bindings.rejects: Choosing earliest start or shortest duration is always optimal.
bindings.reasoning: Intervals [0,3),[1,2),[2,4),[3,5): earliest finish yields a maximum compatible set of two; the exchange preserves feasibility.

theory.title: Dynamic-programming state and recurrence design
theory.reasoning: Define what each state represents, which prior states it depends on, the base cases and the evaluation order, then show that memory reduction preserves those dependencies.

bindings.rejects: A recurrence can omit whether the current item was already used.
bindings.reasoning: Bounded 0/1 knapsack over items (2,3),(3,4),(4,5) at capacity 5: each state is an item prefix and capacity; optimum 7 is checked by subsets.

bindings.rejects: Loop direction does not affect0/1item-use semantics.
bindings.reasoning: One item (2,3) at capacity 4: ascending one-row updates reuse the item and give 6; descending updates give the correct 3.

theory.title: Graph traversal and shortest-path correctness
theory.reasoning: Prove discovery uniqueness, that every edge points forward in a returned order, and the settled-set invariant with its nonnegative-weight premise; certificates must be checked against the graph.

bindings.rejects: Dijkstra is correct whenever no negative cycle exists.
bindings.reasoning: 0->A (2), 0->B (5), B->A (-10): the true distance to A is -5, so settling A at 2 is wrong without any negative cycle.

bindings.rejects: Any DFS output list is a topological order.
bindings.reasoning: Every DAG edge points forward in the returned order; adding 3->0 must produce an explicit cycle failure.

bindings.rejects: Visited only after dequeue never increases pending work.
bindings.reasoning: Mark discovery at enqueue on the diamond with a back edge so each vertex is admitted once.

theory.title: Expected cost and probabilistic guarantees
theory.reasoning: Name the pivot, hash or height model behind an expected bound, separate it from deterministic worst cases, and construct the adversarial or saturated input it does not cover.

bindings.rejects: Ordinary quickselect has deterministic linear worst-case cost.
bindings.reasoning: Expected linear work holds only under the stated pivot model; an adversarial partition sequence is quadratic.

bindings.rejects: A probability formula is a per-query guarantee for arbitrary fixed hashes.
bindings.reasoning: A saturated membership filter answers every query positively; the no-false-negative property holds only without deletion or corruption.

bindings.rejects: Low live load factor implies short probes regardless of tombstones.
bindings.reasoning: Live and occupied-or-deleted counts diverge after deletion; expected probe bounds depend on both and on the hash assumption.
